lens: Cascade integrity, listener idempotency, structural duplication, dead/orphan detection
summary: The notification subsystem is structurally inconsistent and contains massive duplication across three parallel triads (Order/OrderGot/OrderDeliveryBoy) x three channels (Mail/Push/Sms). On top of those nine builder services lives a second, partially overlapping FCM track (SendFcmOn* listeners + SendFcmNotificationJob + FcmNotificationService) introduced by PHASE-36-P1 but never reconciled with the legacy FirebaseService path. Two PHP classes today both purport to be the FCM client. Listener handle() methods are uniformly defensive (single try/catch + Log::info) but none implement ShouldQueue, so under QUEUE_CONNECTION=sync every order side-effect blocks the HTTP thread on Twilio + SMTP + FCM I/O. Idempotency is not enforced anywhere in the notification layer: there is no per-(order_id, status, channel) guard, so any duplicate event dispatch (CleanupStalePendingKioskOrders re-issue, status oscillation, OrderService::store cascade) silently re-sends Mail + SMS + Push.

findings.title: Duplicate FCM service classes (FirebaseService HTTP v1 OAuth2 + FcmNotificationService legacy server-key) coexist
findings.evidence: FirebaseService::sendNotification() (FirebaseService.php:17-67) loads a ServiceAccountCredentials file from NotificationSetting + Settings::group('notification')->all() then POSTs to https://fcm.googleapis.com/v1/projects/{id}/messages:send with Bearer OAuth token. FcmNotificationService::sendToToken() (FcmNotificationService.php:39-97) POSTs to https://fcm.googleapis.com/fcm/send with Authorization: key=<server_key> from config('services.fcm.server_key') (legacy API). SendFcmNotificationJob::handle() (Jobs/SendFcmNotificationJob.php:73-94) routes through FcmNotificationService. Order*PushNotificationBuilder services (OrderPushNotificationBuilder.php:107-108, OrderGotPushNotificationBuilder.php:67-68, OrderDeliveryBoyPushNotificationBuilder.php:64-65) route through FirebaseService. Same order, same status change, two FCM stacks fire.
findings.impact: Maintenance hazard: a fix on one path leaves the other broken. PHASE-36-P1 comment claims FCM HTTP v1 but the implementation uses legacy server key (deprecated/turned down by Google 2024-06-20 for new senders; existing senders may still work but no SLA). FirebaseService path requires NotificationSetting('notification_fcm_json_file') to resolve to an existing file on disk (FirebaseService.php:71-89), otherwise throws and is caught silently. Net effect: in fresh installs, FCM is silently broken on both tracks.
findings.remediation: Pick ONE FCM client. HTTP v1 (OAuth2 + service account) is the only Google-supported path going forward. Consolidate to FcmNotificationService rewritten to use HTTP v1, delete FirebaseService, point all builders + jobs at the single client. Owner gate required: the migration touches every Order*PushNotificationBuilder.

findings.title: No notification listener implements ShouldQueue under QUEUE_CONNECTION=sync default
findings.evidence: config/queue.php:16 sets default to env('QUEUE_CONNECTION', 'sync'). Only SendResetPasswordNotification.php imports ShouldQueue (line 8) but does NOT add it to the class implements clause and does NOT implement the interface. All 11 other Send*Notification listeners run synchronously in the dispatcher thread. OrderService::store (OrderService.php:552-559) dispatches 6 sequential notification events (SendOrderMail/Sms/Push + SendOrderGotMail/Sms/Push) inside the same request thread. Each listener internally calls SmsManagerService->send (Twilio HTTP), Mail::send (SMTP), FirebaseService->sendNotification (HTTPS + service-account OAuth round-trip).
findings.impact: An order creation HTTP request blocks the worker for 6 x N x I/O latency. With QUEUE_CONNECTION=sync the kiosk payment-confirm path measured in PaymentConfirmFcmFailureTest.php is one example where the side-effect chain caused 35/35 kiosk orders to return 422 in Wave B audit. The fix landed for the FCM job path; the legacy Send*Notification listeners were never converted. Production with sync queue + 5+ recipients = >5s HTTP latency on every order side-effect.
findings.remediation: Make every notification listener implement ShouldQueue + onQueue('notifications') (mirror SendFcmNotificationJob.php:67 pattern). For QUEUE_CONNECTION=sync envs this is a no-op; for redis/database it offloads. Verify after-commit ordering — the F-002 round-3 comment in EventServiceProvider.php:128-143 acknowledges the outbox-first contract must be preserved.

findings.title: Zero idempotency in notification layer — duplicate events re-send Mail+SMS+Push
findings.evidence: Every notification builder (Mail/Push/Sms x Order/OrderGot/OrderDeliveryBoy) constructs identical state-machine method() with no de-duplication key. OrderService dispatches SendOrderMail/Sms/Push at 6 distinct call sites (lines 552-554, 1058-1060, 1368-1370, 1637-1639, 1714-1716, 1858-1860). CleanupStalePendingKioskOrders.php:76-78 ALSO dispatches the same triplet when a stale kiosk order is auto-rejected. No notification record (PushNotification model has no order_id/status fingerprint), no Cache::has() guard, no DB unique constraint.
findings.impact: If OrderStatusChanged fires twice (concurrent retry from outbox replay, customer mobile self-cancel race, manual admin status flip + cron auto-reject), Mail + SMS + FCM all fire twice. Customer receives duplicate 'Your order is ready' messages. Drivers get duplicate assignment SMS. Twilio cost amplification.
findings.remediation: Add per-(order_id, status, channel) Cache::add() guard (TTL 5min) at the top of each Send*Notification listener handle(). Reject duplicate. Mirror IdempotencyKeyMiddleware pattern.

findings.title: Massive code duplication — 9 near-identical NotificationBuilder services with ~81 status-method copies
findings.evidence: OrderMailNotificationBuilder.php:46-67 message() dispatcher + 9 status method copies (pending/confirmation/preparing/prepared/outForDelivery/delivered/canceled/rejected/returned) each fetching the same NotificationAlert + identical SwitchBox::ON check + identical Mail::to(...)->send(new OrderMail(...)). OrderSmsNotificationBuilder.php:50-71 + 86-156 identical structure with $code/$phone wrapper. OrderPushNotificationBuilder.php:75-96 + 114-184 identical with $fcmTokenArray. Same 9-method shape repeated. The OrderGot* triad shares no inheritance with the Order* triad. OrderDeliveryBoy* triad only implements the `101` (deliveryBoyAssign) status — fragile magic number, never enum'd.
findings.impact: ~700 LOC of cross-class duplication. Any change to status mapping (e.g. add OrderStatus::REFUNDED) must be applied 9 times. Bug surface area scales linearly; tests scale linearly.
findings.remediation: Extract a single NotificationDispatcher service with channel-strategy injection: (channel: 'mail'|'sms'|'push', audience: 'customer'|'admin'|'delivery_boy', status: OrderStatus). One method, one NotificationAlert lookup, one fan-out. Owner gate (large refactor) — defer V1.0.2.

findings.title: Dead listener + event pair: app/Listeners/SendEmailVerificationNotification + app/Events/SendEmailVerification
findings.evidence: EventServiceProvider.php:80 imports `Illuminate\Auth\Listeners\SendEmailVerificationNotification` (last use wins on collision). EventServiceProvider.php:91-93 maps `Illuminate\Auth\Events\Registered => SendEmailVerificationNotification` — that name resolves to the framework class, NOT app/Listeners/SendEmailVerificationNotification. The app-level App\Events\SendEmailVerification event has NO mapping in $listen[]. grep across /app/ for 'App\Listeners\SendEmailVerification' returned empty. Both files are unreferenced.
findings.impact: Dead code — 60+ LOC across two files. Risk: a future developer adds `App\Events\SendEmailVerification::dispatch(...)` expecting it to send mail, nothing fires.
findings.remediation: Delete app/Listeners/SendEmailVerificationNotification.php AND app/Events/SendEmailVerification.php OR add explicit mapping in EventServiceProvider $listen[App\Events\SendEmailVerification::class] = [App\Listeners\SendEmailVerificationNotification::class] AND fully-qualify the import. Recommendation: delete (the Illuminate Registered path is sufficient).

findings.title: Dual FCM firing on every order status change
findings.evidence: OrderService.php:1637 dispatches SendOrderPush (legacy FirebaseService path, user-tokens, single device targeting). Line 1643 dispatches OrderStatusChanged, which fans out to SendFcmOnOrderStatusChange (FcmNotificationService topic path, kitchen_branch_{id} + customer_order_{orderId} + oss_branch_{id}). For PREPARED state, both customer_order_{N} FCM (topic) and the user's device_token FCM (legacy v1) fire — duplicate notification to customer.
findings.impact: Customer receives 2 push notifications for one status change. UX confusing; Twilio-style 'invisible cost' for FCM (still costs CPU + bandwidth + Google quota).
findings.remediation: Choose one fan-out strategy (topic OR device-token). Recommendation: topic-only via the SendFcm* track, deprecate the Order*PushNotificationBuilder legacy path.

findings.title: 5 Mailable classes map 1:1 to 5 mail templates — no orphan templates
findings.evidence: 5 Mailable classes, 5 templates, 1:1 mapping verified. No orphan templates in resources/views/emails/.
findings.impact: Clean state — mandate explicitly addresses this and is satisfied.

v1_0_1_backlog_disambiguation: The BRAIN V1.0.1 mention of '6 listeners idempotency restants (Catalog/Coupon/Availability×3/Table)' refers to Persist*ToOutbox listeners under sister F-1 / F-2 outbox scope, NOT the Send*Notification listeners audited here. F-8 notification listeners have a SEPARATE idempotency gap that is not tracked in any current BRAIN backlog entry — surface this gap so the orchestrator does not double-count.
